The oxide-reinforced HEA exhibits an excellent combination of YS 821 MPa, UTS 1009 MPa and fracture elongation 28.5% at room temperature. Moreover, its strength has good thermal stability at temperatures up to 800 ◦C. Theoretical calculation reveals that the increased YS is all related to the presence of the oxide particles and is specifically due to the enhanced hardening effects of the dislocation and grain boundary.
